definitions.explanation: The first frost that appears in autumn or early winter, marking the transition to cold weather. An important seasonal marker in Japan.

examples.japanese: {今朝|けさ}{初霜|はつしも}が{降|お}りた。
examples.english: The first frost fell this morning.

examples.japanese: {初霜|はつしも}の{知|し}らせが{届|とど}くと{冬|ふゆ}の{訪|おとず}れを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: When news of the first frost arrives, you can feel winter approaching.

examples.japanese: {初霜|はつしも}が{降|お}りる{前|まえ}に{庭|にわ}の{植物|しょくぶつ}を{室内|しつない}に{入|い}れなければならない。
examples.english: I need to bring the garden plants indoors before the first frost.

notes:
{初霜|はつしも} refers to the first frost of the season, marking the onset of cold weather. Compound of {初|はつ} (first) + {霜|しも} (frost).

SEASONAL SIGNIFICANCE:
A {季語|きご} (seasonal word) associated with late autumn in haiku poetry. Weather services report the date of {初霜|はつしも} each year as a seasonal milestone, and the timing varies by region.

COMMON PATTERNS:
The verb used with frost is {降|お}りる (to descend/fall): {初霜|はつしも}が{降|お}りる (the first frost falls).

RELATED SEASONAL FIRSTS:
- {初雪|はつゆき}: first snow of the season
- {初氷|はつごおり}: first ice of the season
- {初日|はつひ}の{出|で}: first sunrise of the new year

PRACTICAL NOTE:
Gardeners pay close attention to {初霜|はつしも} because frost-sensitive plants must be protected or brought indoors before it arrives.
